title: Yoga Luz · example made with Neblla
hero_sub: Example studio · Calle de Fuencarral 45 · Madrid
notice: This is an example website, made with Neblla so you can see how a real yoga school works. You come in as a student: sign up, book, write to the teacher and buy whatever you like. Payments will be test payments: use the card 4242 4242 4242 4242, any future date and any CVC, nothing is charged. They are not active yet: for now you can look at everything, but not buy.
cover_alt: A student meditates sitting on the mat, in the studio
about_p1: Yoga Luz is a small studio in the centre of Madrid. Ana opened it in 2019 with a simple idea: small-group classes, up to 12 people, where the teacher knows your name and corrects your posture.
about_p2: We are two teachers, Ana and Marcos. We teach Hatha, calm and for all levels, and Vinyasa, more dynamic, from Monday to Saturday. If you have never done yoga, start with Hatha: you don't need to be flexible, just come in comfortable clothes.
studio_hint: This is what our rooms and classes look like. Tap a photo to see it big and find out what it is.
how_1: Sign up for a timetable in “Schedule”, for example Tuesdays and Thursdays at 18:00. You pay every month and your spot is booked in all those classes.
how_2: Or come whenever you like with a 10-class pass: in “Calendar” you pick each single class.
how_3: Private class: one hour alone with your teacher, on the day that suits you.
how_4: Every class has its own chat with your classmates and the teacher, and in Messages you talk privately with the studio.

gallery_dawn_text: Some mornings we start sitting in silence, facing the sun. Five minutes of slow breathing before we move: you feel it all day.
gallery_hall_text: This is where the group classes happen: wooden floor, lots of light, and cushions and blankets for anyone who needs them. In the photo, pigeon pose, which opens the hips.
gallery_moon_text: One knee on the floor and arms up: it stretches the front of the hip, which shortens from sitting so much. We do it in almost every vinyasa class.
gallery_dog_text: The pose you will repeat the most: hands and feet on the mat and hips lifted. It stretches the back and legs. If your heels don't reach the floor, bend your knees: that's fine.
gallery_breath_text: At the end of every class we sit cross-legged with a straight back, and just breathe. It's the part people miss most when they skip it.
gallery_group_text: This is what a Hatha class looks like: up to 12 people, each at their own pace. In the photo, warrior II, legs wide and arms out to the sides, which builds leg strength.
